approachQuestion.prompt:
Interleave the Audit Lines

Two integer arrays left and right contain audit entries. Return a fresh array formed by taking left[0], right[0], left[1], right[1], and so on. Once either array ends, append all remaining entries from the other in their original order.

Example 1: left=[8,9,10], right=[1] → [8,1,9,10].
Example 2: left=[], right=[4,4] → [4,4].
Example 3: left=[2,3], right=[5,6] → [2,5,3,6].

Constraints:
0 ≤ n=left.length,m=right.length ≤ 200,000.
Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Duplicates are separate entries and must be preserved.
Do not modify either array. Return [] when both are empty.
constraints: Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Duplicates are separate entries and must be preserved.
Do not modify either array. Return [] when both are empty.

options.text: Allocate n+m result slots. Copy matching-index pairs up to min(n,m), left first, then copy the remaining suffix from whichever array is longer.
options.feedback: The paired prefix supplies the specified alternation. The tail remains in source order and includes every entry once.

options.text: Make helper copies padded to max(n,m) with a distinct noninteger marker. Interleave the copies, omitting marker entries, into a fresh output array.
options.feedback: A marker outside the integer domain makes this correct even for duplicate values, but the padded copies are avoidable storage.

options.text: Alternate entries only while both arrays have an entry at the current index, then return.
options.feedback: This loses a legal unmatched suffix. [8,9,10] and [1] require [8,1,9,10], not [8,1].

options.text: Concatenate the arrays, then sort all values numerically.
options.feedback: The requested order depends on source and position, not numeric rank. [2] and [1] must produce [2,1], not [1,2].

feedback.reason: Alternation applies while both inputs have entries.
details: Allocate the complete result. Write one left and one right entry for each shared index, then write the longer array’s untouched tail.

Alternation applies while both inputs have entries. Once one ends, append every remaining entry of the other in order. A bound based only on the shorter length loses the unmatched tail, which may contain nearly the whole output.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Copy Pairs Then the Remaining Suffix”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n and m be the lengths. Allocation per slot and indexed reads/writes cost constant time. Include all copying time, even unmatched tails. Exclude input and returned result storage; include helper indices and stack. No helper copies, recursion, hashing or dynamic append are used. Use a bound valid when both inputs are empty.
constraints: Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Duplicates are separate entries and must be preserved.
Do not modify either array. Return [] when both are empty.

options.text: O(n + m + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
O(n + m + 1) time, O(n + m + 1) auxiliary space.
O((n + m + 1)²) time, O(1) auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: Every entry of both inputs is copied, including the longer tail.
details: Every entry is copied exactly once, whether it belongs to a pair or a remaining suffix. Allocation has the same bound, including the constant-cost empty result. Only a fixed number of indices are needed outside returned storage.
The option “O(n + m + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: The complete output contains n+m entries and requires all of them to be copied.
The option “O(min(n,m) + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: This omits the longer input’s suffix, which can dominate the work.
The option “O(n + m + 1) time, O(n + m + 1) auxiliary space.”: The result is excluded and the fixed method creates no padded helpers.
The option “O((n + m + 1)²) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: No entry causes shifting or recopying of an existing prefix.
